newsitem.title: CHINA: China says drives poachers from reserve.
newsitem.headline: China says drives poachers from reserve.

text.p: An anti-poaching campaign in northwestern China has kept hunters from the wild yaks, antelopes and snow leopards that roam the vast zone, the China Daily said on Thursday.
Authorities have caught 83 poachers between October 1995 and May last year in the Hol Xil reserve in a remote corner straddling the regions of Tibet, Qinghai and Xinjiang, the newspaper said.
The tougher measures to protect wildlife in the 90,000 sq km (35,000 sq mile) zone on the Tibetan plateau followed the 1994 killing of a local official in a gun battle with poachers.
That incident shocked local government leaders into action, spurring a drive to stamp out poaching in the area.
Police and ex-soldiers now patrol the zone to protect animals and mineral rights, the newspaper said.
The area's rich natural resources have drawn large numbers of hunters who have killed thousands of animals, endangering the ecological balance, the newspaper said.
